issues.description: Field 'animals' in class Farm: the problem statement (and UML) requires the Farm to aggregate animals using a List<Animal> specifically implemented with an ArrayList and initialized in the no-arg constructor. The solution implementation declares the field as Queue<Animal> animals and initializes it with new LinkedList<>() (and the getter/setter use Queue). This type mismatch (List/ArrayList vs Queue/LinkedList) is present across the artifacts and can confuse students about which collection type and API they must use (e.g., List methods vs Queue methods) and what the constructor must initialize.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent between specification and implementation. Either (A) update the solution to declare the field as private List<Animal> animals and initialize it in the no-arg constructor with new ArrayList<>(), updating getter/setter and methods to use List; or (B) if a FIFO collection was intended, update the problem statement, UML, and tasks to state that a Queue backed by LinkedList is acceptable (and update wording/tests accordingly). Choose one approach and apply it to both the specification and reference solution so students have an unambiguous requirement.
